# FlowSpec

> FlowSpec is a declarative, engine-agnostic specification language for AI-driven acceptance testing. A FlowSpec document describes user journeys (Flows), checkpoints (Cases), semantic interactions (Steps), expected outcomes (Assertions), and captured artifacts (Evidence) — never browser automation. Execution engines (AI browser agents, Playwright, Selenium, mobile agents) decide how to perform the actions.

FlowSpec is to AI acceptance testing what OpenAPI is to REST APIs: a framework-independent source of truth for expected behavior shared by developers, QA engineers, and AI agents.

Key facts:

- Documents are single JSON objects, current spec version 1.0. A project keeps them as plain `.json` files in `.flowspec/` (one per page or area, nestable). The bare filename `.flowspec.json` is the project configuration — `baseUrl`, `targetAttribute`, `output` — never a document. Settings resolve invocation → document → config → default.
- A suite spans multiple pages two ways: `navigate` is an ordinary step so one journey can cross pages, and setup/cleanup exist at both document and flow level (`document setup → flow setup → cases → flow cleanup → document cleanup`) so flows can start on different pages while sharing preconditions.
- Targets are semantic component names resolved via a data attribute — never CSS selectors or XPath. The attribute defaults to `data-constell` and is configurable per document via the top-level `targetAttribute` field, so teams already using `data-testid` or `data-qa` adopt FlowSpec without migrating markup.
- Flows are directed acyclic graphs of cases; omitting `edges` yields an implicit linear chain. `when: "failed"` edges make negative paths (validation errors) passing tests.
- Variables use `{{name}}` interpolation; undefined references fail at load time.
- Case outcomes: passed, failed (assertion), error (step could not execute), skipped (never reached).
- `description` is optional on cases, steps, and assertions and states intent, never mechanics; engines carry it into reports, where an assertion's description becomes its failure message.
- On any failure, engines must capture at least a screenshot and console log.
- Results are written to `flowspec-results/` — `report.json`, optional JUnit `report.xml`, and `evidence/<flow-id>/<case-id>/` artifacts referenced by relative path. Exit codes: 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 errored or invalid document.

## Install

The skill is a single dependency-free Markdown file. Download it directly — `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daveconstell/flowspec/main/public/SKILL.md -o ~/.claude/skills/flowspec/SKILL.md` — or clone `https://github.com/daveconstell/flowspec.git` and run `./install-skill.sh` (no argument installs globally to `~/.claude/skills/` and `~/.agents/skills/`; pass a project path for a project-local install).

## Docs

- [Full specification](/spec-final.md): the complete FlowSpec 1.0 language specification — document format, actions, assertions, evidence, graph model, execution lifecycle, reporting.
- [Authoring skill](/SKILL.md): a condensed skill for writing, reviewing, and running FlowSpec documents. Installed in an agent's skills directory it responds to `/flowspec` commands: `init` (bootstrap `.flowspec.json` and `.flowspec/`), `new <journey>` (author a document), `review [file]`, `run [file] [--url X]`, `add <journey> <file>`, `targets [file]` (resolve every target against the source), and `spec <topic>`.
